title: Do you really have to disclose the use of AI in steam?
author: WildRoach
selftext:
I've been recently browsing steam and stumbled across a lot of quite popular games that CLEARLY is made using ai (the same egg-shaped graphics, same 8 bit sfx, just like opus 5.5 is making) that don't have any ai disclosure.

Here is an example - [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5458210/How\_They\_Built\_the\_Pyramids/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5458210/How_They_Built_the_Pyramids/) (no ad)

I don't see any review bombing whatsoever. So my main point is, why bother disclosing ai usage if people are bad at understanding what is ai and what is not?

comments.author: bluelivezdontmatter
comments.body: There is zero chance of getting "caught" and there's no way of conclusively proving it. Steam is not going to be conducting investigations on every game . It's just not happening. That would mean applying the same standard to AAA studios, which they won't do. Not telling you to violate the rules, but that is the reality

comments.author: VigilanceOne
comments.body:
I mean ok they are lenient for now until they aren't. It's still one of there rules so why even risk it? Also my biggest question why be scared to disclose it anyway? A good game is a good game and will rise above all the noise. (Look at rob run). So why be afraid to tell your customers the truth? 

Think of it from a customer's perspective. If you held strong views against something and someone sold you a product that failed to disclose what that something is because they knew you wouldn't like it how would you feel?

replies.author: tworc2
replies.body: I'm not advocating for anything nor advising anyone to ignore Steam disclosurs. I just said that what OP wrote would be unusually harsh by Steam standards.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
"*It's still one of there* (sic) *rules so why even risk it?*"

Because it got me shitloads more sales...

And yes, my games ARE good (or I wouldn't have sold 143k units of them), but I don't need the likes of you to play a judge over my game because you don't like what tools I used during development.

"If you held strong views against something and someone sold you a product that failed to disclose what that something is because they knew you wouldn't like it how would you feel?"

That's happening on a daily basis... Are you also complaining when your Big Mac doesn't look the same as in the commercials?

People like you are funny, and I take great satisfaction out of probably having sold my games to the likes of you.

replies.author: VigilanceOne
replies.body: If I went to McDonalds and they sold me a big mac that failed to list a controversial ingredient because they thought "It would give them a shitload more sales" That's called a fucking lawsuit.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
Yep, because there can be genuine health consequences associated with that...

Or wait, you're a person that will go into a lifelong depression (or death!) once you accidentally play a game which was partially made with AI? LOL!

comments.author: UglyGarbage68
comments.body: I mean steam is asking that you do so. Customers are asking that you do so. Don't you think you should disclose the capacity you used ai if you did? Be honest and let people vote with their wallets. A vegan has the right to know if the food they eat contains meat.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
Comparing it to a vegan is intellectually dishonest.

And no, my customers DON'T have the right to know what tools I use in my development workflow.

What's next "Well, you have to disclose your political views before you can publish your game on Steam." <- and yes, that's as idiotic as comparing it to veganism...

replies.author: UglyGarbage68
replies.body:
I used that analogy because I was going to compare to cage free eggs but veganism seemed more relatable. The point I'm making is that the people buying the product are asking for information regarding the product. I think its important to be honest. If no one is asking than sure by all means don't bother disclosing.

The spirit of the question op asked is whether its okay to withhold ai usage because disclosing it is possibly determental to sales. I get that it is upsetting "leaving money on the table" so to speak but its dishonest to lie about disclosure the same way it would be dishonest to say something used recycled plastic when you didn't. It's about integrity. 

The only issue I take your response is the analogy that ai use is analogous to polical leanings. A developers personal ideology does not have a direct role in shaping a game. 

The ai usage issue I think will remain even as the tech becomes more ubiquitous in the industry. I think people will expect more transparency similar to what we have seen across industries regarding 3rd world labor, green initiatives and the like.

Its the wild west now but I am sure in the coming years we will see a middle ground. Games will have ai disclosures akin to GMO disclosures on food. No one cares unless its egregious like 90% artificial.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
"*A developers personal ideology does not have a direct role in shaping a game.*"

LOL, wut?! Hahaha.

"*I think people will expect more transparency similar to what we have seen across industries regarding 3rd world labor, green initiatives and the like.*"

So why aren't you demanding those things now?  
FYI though: My games was not made by a team of Indians, nor did I kill a lot of frogs during development.

Only one.

"*Games will have ai disclosures akin to GMO disclosures on food.*"

LOL!  
No, they won't. If anything, since everybody and your mother will be using it for development, a disclosure loses all its meaning...

"*No one cares unless its egregious like 90% artificial.*"

Was this an analogue to the usage of AI? Because if so, that's provenly false...

comments.author: wholikesgame
comments.body: It literally has the UI of most AI games 😂

replies.author: frigginwizard420
replies.body: what you are seeing is the default font and text styling from the game engine unity, one of many game engines AI tends to use. You will also see a lot of games with generic godot UIs, but that has nothing to do with AI

replies.author: wholikesgame
replies.body: Yeah I’m sure the dark colored urine color scheme was a creative choice too 😂 I’m not against AI. I use it ALL THE TIME. I’m also not going to pretend when there are obvious tells. Remove your bias and you’ll understand.

replies.author: frigginwizard420
replies.body:
I'm not the one being biased, I'm not the one pretending to know something.     
I dont know if they used AI to make those game assets, and neither do you. Its slop either way, and we should not be letting shit like this feed into an already toxic witchhunt

replies.author: wholikesgame
replies.body: There’s no witch hunt. Just observations. Not sure how I’m biased. I already told you I work a ton in AI both hobby and professionally. If it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it’s probably a duck. It doesn’t take a load of mental gymnastics to come to that conclusion.

replies.author: frigginwizard420
replies.body: I also work heavily with AI, and you just defined what a bias is in your own self description. You dont know, but based on what you do know you are sure, its literally a text book example of bias

replies.author: wholikesgame
replies.body: It’s called pattern recognition. Theres obvious patterns in that game that give me confidence to form my opinion. You’re just making excuses. Not sure why. 🤷

replies.body: This is unbelievably obvious Claude UI. If you know you know. It's not the styling that makes it obvious, it's the text.

replies.author: saitm
replies.body: Ok but we can’t predict the future. So anyone not disclosing should do it at their own risk

replies.body:
Yeah, of course it's a risk: both by possibly, but doubtfully, getting removed from Steam as well as reputational risk...

But I'm quite sure I made a lot more sales by not disclosing it on my own two games...

replies.author: saitm
replies.body: I believe it. Hopefully this whole prejudice ends soon.

comments.author: MessageSelfdestructs
comments.body:
You believe wrong...

There's some watermarking for text (though there's several workarounds), and also for images, but again, there's easy workarounds for that too.

And with easily available tools to remove watermarks, relying on these watermarks to determine if something is created by AI or not is ignorant.

comments.author: MessageSelfdestructs
comments.body:
I've released two games in the past 2 years, but with around 30% assets created by AI (but I spent a lot of time polishing it so the obvious tells aren't there anymore).

I got one accusation of AI use, and the funny thing? As an example, they gave one sprite that I made completely by myself, without any use of AI. LOL!

replies.author: sarvothtalem
replies.body: im making my first game right now and the demo is done, but, im hiring humans to remake the assets so i can try and get away from saying AI use. It sucks. According to Claude, even an accusation could turn off sales. Apparently admitting to AI cuts around 50 percent of potential sales, or so Claude tells me.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
I seriously doubt it's 50%...

And yeah, remaking the assets, or at least polishing them, is what I did myself, but not out of a "Oh no, I don't want to be found out!", but more because I'm a perfectionist, and I don't think that most AI output today is production-ready.

Get fucked.

comments.author: throwaway098242
comments.body:
Do you know that these AI detectors don't work by definition?

Generative AI is literally trained to generate data such that it's indistinguishable from human work, and this distinguishing is done by a detector that gets trained at the same time as the model gets trained. If you've found an AI detector that reliably detects AI, it would mean you have a detector that is better than what the AI companies are training their models with... That's not physically impossible, but it won't be the case for a AI detection tool you can find on the internet.

comments.body: No.  You don't have to disclose anything.  Valve doesn't disclose which games use DRM.  Valve requires people disclose 3rd party DRM, yet they don't disclose a single game using Steam-DRM.  If Valve isn't going to hold themselves up to any tagging standard, neither do you need to tag things that are market negatives.
